our_denominator: 840 Greek adults who completed an online questionnaire distributed nationwide via email and social media (approx. 3,000 recipients contacted)
their_note: Excluded: the paper measures respondents’ perceived reliability of war information, not a quantitative misinformation share (belief/discernment-only design).
our_flag: borderline; loc: Section 3.3 'Participants' Perspectives on the Veracity of Information', p. 840; Non-probability online convenience sample (email + Viber/Facebook/Messenger to ~3,000 recipients, 840 completions); the authors themselves note the sample does not represent the Greek population on education and age >55. The 'not in favour' bloc includes the neutral midpoint, so this is a permissive reading of 'perceived unreliable'. The strict disagree-only share (41.6%) is a cross-category sum and is therefore NOT reported per R8. The Discussion misstates the same result as '75% of respondents partly or strongly agreed with the statement in question', which is inconsistent with Section 3.3 where 24.9% agreed that the information was reliable; the Section 3.3 wording is authoritative.

our_denominator: 800 social media posts (200 per platform) shortlisted by k-nearest-neighbour similarity to 3 seed MOUD myths from 19,953,599 opioid-related posts on Twitter, YouTube, Reddit and Drugs-Forum
their_note: Excluded machine-learning/classifier detection pipeline; no eligible prevalence/share estimate.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Methods, 'Mixed Methods Approach to Identify Social Media Posts Relevant to MOUD Myths', p. 3; The denominator is a myth-seeded, rank-truncated shortlist, so this is not a prevalence of misinformation among opioid-related posts; it is the yield of the detection pipeline. The numerator counts only NEW myths: posts judged merely relevant to the 3 seed myths are excluded from the 303, so the share of the 800 that carry any misinformation is higher and is not reported. Data collected 2018-2019; year set to the end of the collection window. Country not stated: the platforms and lexicon (DEA street names, US National Survey references) are US-oriented, but no post-level geolocation is applied.

our_denominator: 300 Instagram posts (the top 10 English-language posts per day for 10 days for each of #hoax, #governmentlies and #plandemic, 100 per hashtag)
their_note: The paper’s theme table uses 135/463 = 29.1%; 45.0% incorrectly uses the 300-post collection count.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Discussion, p. 576, first paragraph; underlying counts in Results 'General themes' p. 574 and Table 1; Denominator choice matters here. The Results section reports theme counts against 463 THEME CODES (conspiracy theories n = 135/463, 29.1 percent), because a post could receive several themes; the Discussion reports the same themes against the 300 POSTS (general mistrust 67.6 percent, conspiracy theories 45.0 percent). The post-level figure is the interpretable one and is stated verbatim, so 45.0% is the value kept; 135/300 = 45.0% confirms it. denom_selection=curated because the sample is rank-truncated (top 10 per day) and the three hashtags span more than one issue (#hoax and #governmentlies are not COVID-specific). topic=other rather than covid19 because only 127 of the 300 posts (106 directly, 21 by implication) were COVID-19-related; the corpus is general conspiracy/authority-questioning content. No country is stated for the posts (English-language only), hence Global. Borderline for the same reason as any thematic study: posts were coded for theme, not adjudicated true/false against fact-checks.

our_denominator: All citations of the eleven influential CMN-function studies in the most recent year of the record; the full corpus screened was 1,083 citing papers
their_quote: For both sets of studies, the rate of unsupported citations increased with time, rising to ~25% of all citations about CMN structure and almost 50% of citations about CMN function (Fig. 3).
their_note: The paper reports “almost 50%,” not an exact 50%; the extraction turns approximate wording into an exact value.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Section 'CMN citations in the literature are biased towards positive effects of CMNs', p. 507; Fig. 3b; Time series collapsed to the most recent point. 'almost 50%' is the authors' own verbal approximation of a figure endpoint, so the value is softer than the structure row; confidence low. Exact per-year numerator/denominator not printed. Same date caveat as the structure row.

our_denominator: 301 media articles on BC's decriminalization policy
their_quote: Misleading content was identified in 21 % (n = 63/301) of all media articles.
their_note: Misleading content is defined as technically accurate but contextually distorting; QUALITY, not CONTENT.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Results, 'Content accuracy: identifying misinformation and misleading narratives'; Broader-category variant of the 34% misinformation row in the same country x platform cell, hence definition_variant = true. Borderline because the category by definition covers factually accurate content, so it sits between CONTENT falsity and a quality judgement. Misinformation and misleading content are separate codes; an article can carry both, so the two shares must not be summed.

our_denominator: 98 government resources on BC's decriminalization policy
their_quote: Minimal misleading content was identified in government resources, with only one instance (n = 1/98; 1 %) observed.
their_note: The paper defines this as factually accurate but contextually distorting misleading content; under the rules this is QUALITY, not CONTENT.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Results, 'Content accuracy: identifying misinformation and misleading narratives - Government resources'; Broader-category variant of the misinformation row in the same country x platform cell, hence definition_variant = true. Flagged borderline because a wholly accurate item can receive the 'misleading' label (the category is defined as factually accurate content presented in a distorting way), which the protocol treats as closer to a quality judgement than to falsity. Full sentence: 'Minimal misleading content was identified in government resources, with only one instance (n = 1/98; 1 %) observed.' The two-column extraction splits it across interleaved lines, so only the contiguous fragment is quoted.

our_denominator: 1,273,930 Italian-language comments on COVID-19 YouTube videos, posted 15/01/2020-15/06/2020
their_note: Comments on questionable channels are CONTENT, not sharing acts.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Table 1, p. 5 (Methods, Data collection); Coded SHARING/content_share because the denominator is engagement acts (comments), not items that exist: the share measures how much of the commenting activity in this corpus went to questionable sources. The comments themselves were not judged for veracity; the label is inherited from the channel. borderline=true because commenting is engagement rather than resharing.

our_denominator: 314 spider-related media reports published in Italian online newspapers 2010-2020 and referring to human-spider encounters in Italy
their_quote: One or more error types were present in 73% of media reports (Figure 3).
their_note: Scientific-quality/error measure; QUALITY, not CONTENT.
our_flag: loc: Results §3.2 Quality of media reports, p. 1151; also Abstract point 3 ('The news quality was generally poor: 70% contained different types of error, 32% were sensationalistic, and in virtually none was an expert consulted.') and Discussion §4.1 p. 1153; The paper reports two different values for the same quantity: 73% in the Results and 70% in the Abstract and Discussion. 73% is taken as the value because it is the Results-section figure; the discrepancy is unresolved in the text (73% of 314 = 229 reports, 70% = 220). Year of data collection recorded as 2020 (search/extraction period); the articles themselves span 2010-2020.

our_denominator: 400 randomly sampled Parler posts ('parleys') carrying #COVID19Vaccine or #NoCovidVaccine, drawn from a larger pool of ~7,000 COVID-19-vaccine parleys
their_quote: Thematic analysis reveals five key themes: reasons to refuse the COVID-19 vaccine (40%), side effects of the COVID-19 vaccine (28%), population control through the COVID-19 vaccine (23%), children getting vaccinated without parental consent (5%), and comparison of other health issues with COVID-19 (2%).
their_note: The paper reports thematic prevalence in Parler posts, not externally truth-judged misinformation prevalence; this is not CONTENT under the stated construct rule.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Abstract, p. 1; repeated in Findings section 3 (p. 5) and elaborated in section 3.3 'COVID-19 Vaccine as a Population Control Mechanism' (p. 7); Borderline for three reasons. (1) The 23% is a THEMATIC share, not a falsity judgement: posts were coded for what they were about, not graded true/false against a ground truth. The theme itself, however, is a specific false claim (microchips / enzymes in the vaccine for population control), which is why it is coded CONTENT rather than QUALITY. (2) The other four themes (vaccine refusal 40%, side effects 28%, children vaccinated without consent 5%, comparison with other diseases 2%) are NOT falsity-defined categories and were not extracted; the paper itself treats some of them as legitimate concerns ('users raise important and legitimate concerns about vaccine efficacy'). (3) No country is stated for the sampled posts; the paper's framing is U.S. (2020 U.S. election, Parler's U.S. user base), but at least one quoted parley is about Canada, so country_norm is set to Global. Year of data collection spans Nov 2020 to Jan 2021; 2020 recorded as the start year.

our_denominator: the 20 most-posted news sites in the 6 liberal subreddits
their_quote: In contrast, the equivalent number for liberal subreddits is 20%.
their_note: The 20% is the share of top news-site sources with mixed-or-lower factual ratings, not the share of links or sharing activity.
our_flag: loc: Results, 'Effect of ideology on COVID-19 news source accuracy', p. 9 (Figure 4); Rank-truncated top-20 set.

our_denominator: the 20 most-posted news sites in the 6 conservative subreddits
their_quote: Of the top 20 news sites posted in conservative subreddits, 60% had mixed or lower factual ratings.
their_note: The denominator is the top 20 news sites, and the outcome is their external factual-rating classification; this is CONTENT, not sharing acts.
our_flag: loc: Results, 'Effect of ideology on COVID-19 news source accuracy', p. 9 (Figure 4); Rank-truncated top-20 set, hence denom_selection=curated; a broader definition of unreliable (mixed or lower) than the NewsGuard flagged-site rows.

our_denominator: 954 English-language original tweets containing a COVID-19 data visualisation whose text opposes conventional measures (masks, lockdowns, vaccination) or denies the existence or severity of the crisis, out of 9,958 manually coded COVID-19 visualisation tweets
their_note: Reasoning-error/quality measure; QUALITY, not CONTENT.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Figure 6 (Results of qualitative coding by polarity), Section 4.2; Denominator is a stance-defined stratum of the corpus (opinion tweets opposing measures), not the whole corpus; the paper reports no overall share of the 9,958 posts that are misleading, and summing the three polarity strata would be a computed cross-category sum barred by R8. borderline=true because the ground truth is reasoning quality of the poster's argument rather than the falsity of a claim against an external verification, so a post with a defensible conclusion could still be coded as containing a reasoning error. Data collection spans 15 May 2020 to 6 September 2021; year recorded as 2020 (start of streaming). Corpus is worldwide English-language Twitter, so no country is stated.

our_denominator: 517 English-language original tweets containing a COVID-19 data visualisation whose text supports conventional measures and government intervention, out of 9,958 manually coded COVID-19 visualisation tweets
their_note: The 62.1% is reasoning-error/deceptiveness coding; a true visualization could still be labeled misleading, so this is quality/deception rather than external truth-judged CONTENT.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Figure 6 (Results of qualitative coding by polarity), Section 4.2; The counterpart stratum to the measure-opposing row: the paper's headline point is that misleading reasoning is present on both sides of the COVID-19 argument, though far more prevalent among measure-opposing posts (94.8% vs 62.1%). Same borderline and ground-truth caveats as the measure-opposing row.

our_denominator: 96 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 1 ("The oldest users with low SM literacy"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
their_note: Intentional sharing is SHARING, not RECALL.
our_flag: loc: p. 180, Table 5 (Sharing of fake news, by latent class); class sizes in Table 4 (p. 179); The paper reports NO pooled prevalence of self-reported fake-news sharing: the only shares with denominators are the six latent-class (social-media-literacy class) cells of Table 5. Class sizes are from Table 4 (N 96/65/126/265/383/65 = 1,000) and reproduce every Table 5 percentage as an exact part/whole share (e.g. 29.23%% x 65 = 19; 50.77%% x 65 = 33), confirming the denominators. A pooled figure would require summing across classes (forbidden by R8), so all six class rows are recorded. These are subgroups of one survey, not independent samples - pool with care. Year of data collection spans Dec 2019-Jan 2020; 2019 recorded as the start year.

our_denominator: 383 Polish active Facebook news users in latent class 5 ("The youngest, heavy SM users with average SM literacy"); total sample 1,000 recruited from the largest Polish research panel
their_note: Intentional sharing is SHARING, not RECALL.
our_flag: loc: p. 180, Table 5 (Sharing of fake news, by latent class); class sizes in Table 4 (p. 179); The paper reports NO pooled prevalence of self-reported fake-news sharing: the only shares with denominators are the six latent-class (social-media-literacy class) cells of Table 5. Class sizes are from Table 4 (N 96/65/126/265/383/65 = 1,000) and reproduce every Table 5 percentage as an exact part/whole share (e.g. 29.23%% x 65 = 19; 50.77%% x 65 = 33), confirming the denominators. A pooled figure would require summing across classes (forbidden by R8), so all six class rows are recorded. These are subgroups of one survey, not independent samples - pool with care. Year of data collection spans Dec 2019-Jan 2020; 2019 recorded as the start year.

our_denominator: 8,405 respondent-by-item exposure instances (Japanese online panel respondents aged 15-69, main survey N = 5,000, counted once per piece of misinformation they had encountered; non-exposed pairs are not in the analysis)
their_note: The paper reports a mean of 0.174, not a percentage share; percentages of means are not shares.
our_flag: loc: p. 129, Table 2 (Basic statistics of the panel data); Denominator is exposure instances (person x item), not persons, so this is not a share of respondents; a person exposed to several claims contributes several observations. The main-survey sample was deliberately over-sampled on people who had encountered misinformation ("As the screening stage included a higher proportion of individuals exposed to misinformation, the sample distribution in this study is skewed compared to the real-world population"), and Table 2 does not state whether the reported means are weighted, so the 17.4% is likely to overstate the population figure. The 15 claims span five topic areas, hence topic = other. Panel is an opt-in internet monitor panel (My Voice.com) with sex-by-age allocation. ground_truth is self_report because the numerator is the respondent's own report of dissemination; the veracity of the items themselves was set by fact-checking organisations (see ground_truth_detail).

our_denominator: 240 English-language TikTok videos about LASIK, LASEK or SMILE with over 1000 views, sampled a fixed number per LRS hashtag in January 2025
their_quote: One video (0.4%) contained potentially harmful misinformation.
their_note: Checked against the paper; value, denominator and construct match.
our_flag: loc: Results, section 3.1 Video Characteristics, p. 4 of 9; also Abstract (Results) and Discussion; Denominator is curated: a fixed number of videos was taken per hashtag from the platform's search ranking, with a >1000-view threshold, so the sample is of popular topical videos rather than a random draw. The falsity judgement is a single subjective grader call with no external ground truth, so the 0.4% is a lower bound on inaccurate content by any stricter definition; the authors themselves say 'Misinformation was rarely overt; only one video was flagged as potentially harmful' but that 'omission bias was pervasive'.

our_denominator: the 20 most-posted news sites in the 6 conservative subreddits
their_quote: Using NewsGuard, five (25%) of the top 20 sites shared by conservatives “severely violate basic journalistic standards.”
their_note: Exact top-20 share.
our_flag: loc: Results, 'Effect of ideology on COVID-19 news source accuracy', p. 9; Robustness-check rating service (NewsGuard rather than MediaBiasFactCheck) on the same curated top-20 set; the equivalent liberal figure is stated as zero but with no percentage, so no liberal row was created.

our_denominator: 87 Turkish-language YouTube videos on diabetic foot care retained from the 200 videos returned by the keyword search (exclusions: not about diabetic foot care, no audio, advertising content, duplicates, not in Turkish, herbal products)
their_quote: 6.9% not useful, while 4.6% contained misleading information.
their_note: Checked against the cited passage; value, denominator and construct match.
our_flag: loc: Abstract (Results) p. 430; repeated in Results section 3, p. 431; The misleading-information flag is separate from the usefulness/DISCERN/GQS scoring, so it is coded CONTENT rather than QUALITY, but the paper never defines what counted as misleading and reports no reliability for this specific judgement, hence medium confidence. 4.6% of 87 corresponds to 4 videos; the paper gives no count. Note 4.6% also appears elsewhere in the paper as the share of distracting factors related to video length and as the share of videos from medical websites.

our_denominator: All citations of the seven influential CMN-structure studies in the most recent year of the record; the full corpus screened was 593 citing papers
their_quote: For both sets of studies, the rate of unsupported citations increased with time, rising to ~25% of all citations about CMN structure and almost 50% of citations about CMN function (Fig. 3).
their_note: Checked against the cited passage; value, denominator and construct match.
our_flag: borderline; loc: Section 'CMN citations in the literature are biased towards positive effects of CMNs', p. 507; Fig. 3a; Time series collapsed to the most recent point, as reported verbatim in the text ('rising to ~25%'). The value is the authors' own approximation read off Fig. 3a; the exact per-year numerator and denominator are not printed in the text. borderline=true because the corpus is scientific citations rather than public-facing content, and because the reported value is approximate. Data-collection/search date is in Supplementary Note 2, which is not part of this text file; year set to the publication-record year 2022 (manuscript received 18 August 2022).

our_denominator: Videos in the 200-video sample discoverable only with medical search terms; the exact subset size is not reported
their_quote: 45.3% of videos discoverable using colloquial search terms contained misinformation, whereas only 20.5% of videos only discoverable using medical search terms contained misinformation (P < 0.001).
their_note: Checked against the paper; value, denominator and construct match.
our_flag: loc: Abstract (Results) and Results p. 18; Companion row to the colloquial-search-term estimate; same denominator-not-printed limitation.

our_denominator: Videos in the 200-video sample discoverable with the colloquial search terms 'appendix surgery' or 'gallbladder surgery'; the exact subset size is not reported (search-criterion counts, which overlap across terms, are appendix surgery 50 and gallbladder surgery 67)
their_quote: 45.3% of videos discoverable using colloquial search terms contained misinformation, whereas only 20.5% of videos only discoverable using medical search terms contained misinformation (P < 0.001).
their_note: Checked against the paper; value, denominator and construct match.
our_flag: loc: Abstract (Results) and Results p. 18; Kept because the colloquial-vs-medical contrast is a headline result reported in the abstract, not a demographic subgroup. Confidence medium only because the denominator of the subset is never printed: Table 1 gives per-search-criterion counts that sum past 200 (videos are discoverable by several terms), so the subset size cannot be reconstructed. definition_variant=false: this is a sampling subset of the same misinformation definition, not a stricter or broader definition.

our_denominator: 200 YouTube videos (the 100 most-viewed for each of appendectomy and cholecystectomy, retrieved with six search terms)
their_quote: More than a third (35%) of videos contained misinformation. Doctors, medical education, and healthcare systems published videos with less misinformation, whereas patients, health/wellness groups published more misinformation (P < 0.001). [Results p. 18 restates it: "Sixty five percent of videos did not contain misinformation, while 21.5% of videos contained some misinformation and 13.5% of videos contained more significant misinformation."]
their_note: Checked against the abstract and results sentence reporting more than a third of videos.
our_flag: loc: Abstract (Results); Results p. 18; Table 2; 35% is stated verbatim in the abstract and reproduced exactly by Table 2 (70/200). denom_selection=curated because the sample is the top-100 most-viewed per procedure. Country left Global: the search was in English with no stated geographic restriction, although the authors are US-based and frame the procedures as the most common EGS procedures in the United States. Data-collection date is not reported anywhere in the text; year set to the submission year 2022 and flagged.
